name: Possession
simpleText: How much of the ball a team has.
exploreText: Possession share is usually measured from passes or time on the ball. Having more of the ball does not guarantee more chances.
advancedText: Touchline uses pass-based possession: a team's attempted passes divided by all attempted passes.
misconceptions: More possession means a team played better.

name: Possession chain
simpleText: One spell on the ball, from winning it to losing it.
exploreText: A chain links every action a team makes until the opponent takes the ball, play stops for a change of possession, or the half ends.
advancedText: Chains follow the provider's possession number; a chain's end type is shot, goal, turnover, out, foul or half end.

name: Build-up
simpleText: How a team moves the ball out from the back.
exploreText: Teams can build up patiently with short passes through defenders and midfielders, or go long to skip the press.
advancedText: Build-up success = share of own-third possessions that reach the final third.
misconceptions: Long balls are always a sign of poor build-up.

name: Progressive pass
simpleText: A pass that moves the ball a lot closer to the opponent's goal.
exploreText: A progressive pass gains a meaningful amount of ground towards goal. The distance needed is larger in your own half than near the opponent's box.
advancedText: Touchline v1: completed open-play pass reducing distance to goal centre by >= 30 m (own half), >= 15 m (crossing halves) or >= 10 m (opponent half).

name: Line-breaking pass
simpleText: A pass that goes past a line of opposing players.
exploreText: Line-breaking passes skip a defensive or midfield line, putting the receiver behind those opponents.
advancedText: Detecting lines reliably needs player positions (freeze frames or tracking); Touchline will add this with tracking data.

name: Half-space
simpleText: The channels between the centre and the wings.
exploreText: The pitch can be split into five vertical lanes. The two between the centre and the wings are the half-spaces, hard to defend because they sit between full-backs and centre-backs.
advancedText: Touchline lanes are 13.6 m wide across a 68 m pitch: wide left, half-space left, central, half-space right, wide right.

name: Wide channel
simpleText: The strips of pitch along the touchlines.
exploreText: Teams use the wide channels to stretch the opponent and deliver crosses or cut-backs.
advancedText: Outermost 13.6 m lanes on each side.

name: Zone 14
simpleText: The central area just outside the penalty box.
exploreText: Getting the ball into zone 14 lets a team shoot, play through balls or combine around the box.
advancedText: Touchline v1: x in [70, 87.5) m, y in [22.67, 45.33) m on a 105 x 68 m pitch.

name: Final third
simpleText: The attacking third of the pitch.
exploreText: Entering the final third is a basic step towards creating chances.
advancedText: x >= 70 m on a 105 m pitch.

name: Box entry
simpleText: Getting the ball into the opponent's penalty area.
exploreText: Box entries count possessions where the ball reached the penalty area through a pass, carry or touch.

name: Overload
simpleText: Having more players than the opponent in one area.
exploreText: Overloads create a free player. Teams often overload one side to then switch play to the other.
advancedText: Measuring numerical superiority needs player positions; Touchline infers side preference from progression and xT lanes until tracking arrives.

name: High press
simpleText: Trying to win the ball back near the opponent's goal.
exploreText: A pressing team closes down defenders and the goalkeeper to force mistakes high up the pitch.
advancedText: Event proxies: low PPDA, many high turnovers and a high average defensive-action height.
misconceptions: Pressing high always means winning the ball high.

name: Mid-block
simpleText: Defending from the middle of the pitch.
exploreText: A mid-block lets the opponent have the ball in their own half, then engages around halfway.
advancedText: Typically moderate PPDA and a middling defensive-action height.

name: Low block
simpleText: Defending deep, close to your own goal.
exploreText: A low block protects space behind the defence and in front of goal, accepting less of the ball.
advancedText: Usually high PPDA, few high turnovers, low defensive-action height.
misconceptions: A low block is purely defensive; many low-block teams are dangerous on the counter.

name: PPDA
simpleText: Passes per defensive action: how many passes the opponent makes before you try to win the ball.
exploreText: Lower PPDA usually means more aggressive pressing.
advancedText: Touchline v1: opponent passes in their own 60% / tackles + interceptions + fouls in that area.
misconceptions: PPDA from different sites is directly comparable.

name: Counterpress
simpleText: Pressing immediately after losing the ball.
exploreText: Instead of retreating, players attack the ball straight away to win it back before the opponent organises.
advancedText: Touchline measures regains within 3, 5 and 8 seconds of losing possession.

name: Rest defence
simpleText: The players a team keeps back while attacking.
exploreText: Rest defence protects against counter-attacks when the ball is lost.
advancedText: Assessing rest defence structure needs tracking data (Milestone 4).

name: Transition
simpleText: The moments right after the ball changes teams.
exploreText: Transitions are when teams are least organised, so fast attacks and quick regains matter.
advancedText: Touchline links transition metrics to possession chains and play patterns.

name: Expected goals (xG)
simpleText: How likely a shot is to be a goal.
exploreText: xG rates each chance from 0 to 1 using its location, angle, body part and situation. Summing xG shows how many goals a team's chances were worth.
advancedText: Touchline shows the provider's xG model (StatsBomb). Single-match differences between goals and xG are noisy.
misconceptions: xG predicts the result of a single match.

name: Expected assists (xA)
simpleText: The xG of the shots a pass created.
exploreText: xA credits the passer with the quality of the chance they set up.
advancedText: Sum of xG of shots whose key pass was by the player.

name: Expected threat (xT)
simpleText: How much a pass or dribble increased the chance of scoring soon.
exploreText: xT values each pitch area by how often having the ball there leads to a goal. Moving the ball to a more valuable area adds threat.
advancedText: Static 12x8 grid by Karun Singh; action value = xT(end) - xT(start).
misconceptions: xT measures shot quality (that is xG).

name: Formation
simpleText: The basic shape a team lines up in, such as 4-3-3.
exploreText: Formations change in and out of possession and after substitutions; they are a starting point, not the whole story.
advancedText: Recorded from Starting XI and Tactical Shift events.
misconceptions: A team's formation stays fixed all match.

name: Inverted full-back
simpleText: A full-back who moves into midfield when the team has the ball.
exploreText: Instead of overlapping on the wing, the full-back steps inside to add a midfielder and protect against counters.
advancedText: Role profile archetype 'inverted fullback' uses central involvement and passing volume from a full-back position.

name: False nine
simpleText: A centre-forward who drops into midfield.
exploreText: A false nine pulls centre-backs out of position and creates space for runners.
advancedText: Detected from forward position group with deep average position and high passing involvement.

name: Double pivot
simpleText: Two holding midfielders side by side.
exploreText: A double pivot gives security in build-up and protection in front of the defence.
advancedText: Seen in formations such as 4-2-3-1 and 4-2-2-2.

name: Third-man run
simpleText: A run that receives a pass after a quick combination between two teammates.
exploreText: Player A passes to B, who plays it first time to C making the run; the run is hard to track because the defender watches A and B.
advancedText: Needs sequence detection plus positions; planned with pattern discovery.

name: Passing network
simpleText: A map of who passed to whom.
exploreText: Lines between players show the most common passing links; node positions show where players usually received or passed.
advancedText: Nodes = mean pass start/end locations; edges = completed passes between pairs.

name: Set piece
simpleText: Corners, free kicks and throw-ins.
exploreText: Set pieces are rehearsed routines and can be a large share of a team's chances.
advancedText: Touchline groups possessions by play pattern (From Corner, From Free Kick, From Throw In).

name: Compactness
simpleText: How close together a team's players are.
exploreText: Compact teams leave little space between lines; it needs player tracking to measure.
advancedText: Planned with tracking (Milestone 4).

name: Player role
simpleText: What a player actually did, beyond their listed position.
exploreText: Two midfielders in the same position can play very different roles, such as ball-winner or playmaker.
advancedText: Touchline compares a player's per-90 actions with 14 role archetypes and shows the closest two.

name: Score state
simpleText: Whether a team was leading, drawing or trailing.
exploreText: Teams often change approach depending on the score, so Touchline splits metrics by score state.
advancedText: Each event is labelled from the goal timeline at the moment it happened.
